deviations: yh_data.csv (about 2 GB) read with data.table::fread(select=) of only the 19 columns the claimed specifications use, to fit the sandbox's 300 s / 4 GB limits.

Hiring regressions (Table 1 Panels A/B, Table 2) estimated by weighted least squares on cells of state x month x demo2 x young x prior labour-force status, with the cell weight being the sum of the CPS weights and the outcome being the weighted mean of hired100. Every regressor and fixed effect is constant within a cell, so the point estimates equal those of the person-level aweighted regression; the clustered-SE small-sample factor uses the number of cells instead of persons. The wage regression (Table 10) is run at person level.
Stata's m:1 crosswalk merges are done as lookups on keys deduplicated by (code, code-year).
notes: Followed YH_data_init.do and YH_regs.do: hired2 x 100 outcome, young = potential experience <= 10, youngurate/oldurate interactions, demo2 = group(minority, female, hisp, educ), state + month-year + demo2 fixed effects, CPS weight (v2pwsswgt+pwsswgt)/2, state-clustered SEs, fixef.rm='none'. Sample: exp and state unemployment rate non-missing (N = 16,948,516, matching the paper). Table 10 Panel B col 1: log real weekly wage of new hires with v2prwernal==0, with occupation (2002 recode) and industry (2002 recode) fixed effects (N = 112,858). attempt-1 was an exploratory read/timing run with no RESULT lines. attempt-2 was the first scored run; check_attempt reported every claim within tolerance. The only change after it was printing n_obs_full_sample as an exact integer (%.6g had rounded it to 1.69485e+07). The final run reproduces all 13 claims.
